subject: Novus Health DPA: data enclave scope & subprocessor carveouts - product/security review requested
messages:
From: Sara Martin <sara.martin@novushealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Novus Procurement <procurement@novushealth.com>
Cc: legal-team@novushealth.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Novus DPA - request for data enclave scope carveout and subprocessors list

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our security and legal teams reviewed the standard DPA and have two outstanding asks before procurement can route this for signature:

1) Data enclave / retention scope: we need an explicit carveout that prevents storage of certain runtime artifacts outside our AWS us-west-2 tenant. In particular, Novus cannot allow:
   - persistent KV cache snapshots stored outside our region,
   - post-run embeddings or training artifacts to be retained beyond the session, and
   - any model telemetry that would include patient-identifiable metadata.

2) Subprocessors: we need a complete subprocessors list for the stack that will handle logs, metrics, and backup storage. The list should include names and locations (region/country).

I've attached a marked-up DPA (Novus_DPA_redline_v3.docx) and a CSV export of their current subprocessors (Novus_subprocessors_list.csv). Can your legal/security/product teams confirm whether Redwood can accept these constraints or propose alternative contract language compatible with your runtime?

We are trying to avoid extended vendor review cycles; if we can get an answer by EOD Monday (Aug 23) procurement will proceed.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Martin
Sr. Security PM, Novus Health

Sara — thanks for the clear ask and the redline. Looping in Product (Dev), Legal (Olga), and Security (Hannah + Laura) to validate feasibility and propose contract language.

Quick context for everyone internal: Novus will run inference calls against our hosted API; they are asking for:
- strict regional data residency for KV/cache snapshots and backups (us-west-2 only)
- zero retention of embeddings or training artifacts beyond ephemeral session scope
- disclosure of subprocessors used for logs/metrics/backup with region info

We also need to be explicit about what we can guarantee for hosted customers vs Dedicated/Private. If this needs a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) to be acceptable, call that out.

Action items:
- Dev: please reply with product/implementation constraints and an alternative wording we can offer for hosted customers.
- Legal: please propose contract language that balances buyer requirements and our operational limitations.
- Security: confirm whether KMS/HSM controls and audit logs are sufficient; flag any unacceptable asks.

I attached a short note with my initial take (redline_notes_mina.pdf). I'll consolidate and reply back to Sara once we have alignment.

— Mina
Mina Haddad

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Novus DPA - request for data enclave scope carveout and subprocessors list

On Thu, Aug 20, 2026 at 9:12 AM Sara Martin <sara.martin@novushealth.com> wrote:
> Hi Mina,
> 
> Thanks again for the demo last week...

Team — quick product notes from infra/serving perspective:

Summary of constraints and technical feasibility:
- KV cache snapshots: we do produce periodic cache checkpoints for warm-starting long-running deployments. For hosted customers these checkpoints are stored in our central object store (multi-region replication by default). We can scope retention to a single region for an account, but we do not currently encrypt separate buckets per-account without an enterprise add-on.

- Embeddings/training artifacts: we do not train on customer data in hosted by default. Embeddings generated during a session are ephemeral but may be cached to improve latency under certain caching profiles. We can turn off caching and per-session embedding persistence for a tenant, at a small latency/cost tradeoff.

- Telemetry: anonymized performance telemetry is collected for platform health. We have an option to filter PII fields and to disable certain telemetry categories for an account; full disable may impact our ability to diagnose incidents.

Suggested contract language (hosted-friendly):
"Redwood will not persist user-provided content or derived embeddings beyond the duration necessary to service the request, except as required for operational logs, system metrics, or to meet legal obligations. Customer may request account-level settings to restrict KV cache persistence to Customer's specified region; such settings may incur platform constraints and require a dedicated configuration"

If Novus requires guaranteed zero-copy storage and isolated infrastructure, this would push to Dedicated or Private deployment (we should call that out).

I'll flag two follow-ups: 1) we need to confirm whether Novus' subprocessors include any cross-border backup provider; 2) we should offer a migration path (Dedicated) in the contract if hosted cannot meet their residency needs.

— Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Product Manager, Runtime

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novus DPA - request for data enclave scope carveout and subprocessors list

Team — legal review below. I made inline edits to Novus_DPA_redline_v3 and propose the following compromise clauses to surface in the DPA: 

1) Scoped KV persistence clause (compromise):
"Redwood will, upon Customer request, implement account-scoped persistence controls that limit KV cache snapshot storage to a designated region (e.g., AWS us-west-2). Such controls are subject to Redwood's standard operational requirements and may require an enterprise subscription or Dedicated deployment for guaranteed isolation"

2) Embeddings & derived artifacts:
"Redwood does not train models using Customer-provided input. Generated embeddings and other transient derivatives will not be retained beyond the session except where caching is enabled to improve performance; Customer can request caching to be disabled for their account. Any retained artifacts will be stored in Customer-designated regions when account-scoped persistence controls are enabled."

3) Subprocessors:
"Redwood will provide an up-to-date list of subprocessors and their processing locations. For subprocessors that perform storage/backup, Customer may request additional contractual safeguards (SCCs, subprocessor DPA) or require suppression of certain categories of telemetry."

We should include a short paragraph that enumerates the operational trade-offs (latency/cost/diagnosability) so Novus understands the impacts. Also recommend adding a short SLA carveout that routes critical incident debugging info via a secured channel rather than broad telemetry export.

I need Security confirmation on KMS/HSM and audit-log sufficiency (Laura/Hannah). Once Security signs off, I can push this language back to Novus and suggest the Dedicated migration path as an option if they cannot accept hosted constraints.

— Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Novus DPA - request for data enclave scope carveout and subprocessors list

On Fri, Aug 21, 2026 at 9:45 AM Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — legal review below...

Security response: we can support the proposed scoped persistence clause with the following controls required in the contract or an enterprise attachment:
- Customer-managed KMS keys for data-at-rest encryption (we support AWS KMS integration for Dedicated and hosted with enterprise onboarding).
- Audit log export of access to KV cache snapshots and backup objects retained for more than 24 hours. Logs must include requester identity, object id, and timestamp.
- Prohibit cross-border restore: any restore of backups that contain Customer-associated artifacts must be executed within Customer-designated regions unless explicit written approval is provided.

Operational note: disabling caching for Novus will increase median latency by ~15-25% on conversational workloads and could increase token cost ~8-12% depending on usage patterns. Recommend we add this impact summary to any response to Novus.

If Novus requires stronger guarantees (e.g., no telemetry ingestion whatsoever), we should route to Private deployment or include a robust incident support agreement. Security signs off on the legal language proposed, subject to inclusion of the KMS requirement above and a short operational impact paragraph.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Novus Procurement <procurement@novushealth.com>

Subject: Re: Novus DPA - request for data enclave scope carveout and subprocessors list

Mina / Team — thanks for the quick turnaround and detailed responses. Novus legal reviewed the alternative language (we prefer the scoped persistence clause you proposed) and procurement is prepared to proceed if Redwood agrees to the following as a condition on hosted:

- Implement account-scoped persistence limited to AWS us-west-2 within 30 days of signature
- Enable customer-managed KMS for the account
- Provide the current subprocessors CSV and notify Novus 30 days before onboarding any new storage/backups subprocessor

If Redwood confirms acceptance, we'll prepare the DocuSign packet and sign. If the account-scoped persistence requires an enterprise subscription or Dedicated deployment, please indicate the pricing delta and timeline.

Sara — please confirm next steps for the security checklist on your side; happy to circulate a final copy once we have Redwood's confirmation.

Procurement
Novus Health
